### Ignore fenced code when checking release-note headings

**Severity:** `medium`

**Affected code:** `.github/skills/release-note-generation/scripts/preview-release-body.ps1:Assert-PreviewReleaseBodyLayout`, its draft-creation and verification callers, and `.github/skills/release-note-generation/tests/preview-release.Tests.ps1`.

**Problem:** Both heading regexes scan fenced code as ordinary Markdown. For example, a fenced PowerShell snippet containing `# Print the installed version.` is rejected as a level-one heading; fenced output containing `Status` followed by `======` is rejected too. Neither produces a rendered title, and the same inputs fail inside the correctly ordered managed block.

**Why it matters:** If left unfixed, otherwise valid preview notes containing code examples or diagnostic output can be blocked during draft creation and final verification, even though no duplicate title is present.

**Suggested change:**
1. Make the heading scan ignore fenced-code contents while retaining the existing managed-region boundary.
2. Recognize Markdown backtick and tilde fences, including matching closing-fence lengths, rather than deleting individual lines that happen to contain backticks.
3. Keep rejection of real ATX and Setext level-one headings outside fences. Add regression cases for fenced PowerShell comments and Setext-looking output, alongside the existing true-heading and outside-managed-region cases.

**Verification:** Run the existing preview-release test suite and the new fence cases through the shared assertion. Valid fenced examples must pass; real level-one headings in the managed content must still fail. Exercise the same cases through the draft-creation and final-verification entry points.
proposed_comments.title: Ignore fenced code when checking release-note headings
